title: Moroccan Mint Tea High Pour
summary: In Morocco, green tea is brewed with fresh spearmint and plenty of sugar, then poured from a tall silver pot held high above small glasses. The long fall cools and airs the tea and raises a crown of froth. Here you take the pot and fill a tray of glasses to the line without spilling.
howToPlay: Choose a glass: the pot moves over it and a ring on the rim shows where the stream will land.
Press and hold to tip the pot, and drag to move it. Lift the pot higher as the glass fills to raise the froth.
Move slowly: a hurried hand makes the stream wobble. Flick the pot upward and let go to cut the stream cleanly.
Fill every glass to its dashed line, then press Serve to see your stars.
rules: Each round puts between four and five glasses on the tray, and each glass has a dashed fill line.
The tea flows only while you hold the pot tipped; the pot holds only a little more than the tray needs, so tea spilt on the tray cannot be poured again.
Score out of 100: even fill at the line (34), froth crown (28), a dry tray (18), a steady stream (20).
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40; pouring nothing scores 0.
heritageNote: In Morocco and across the Maghreb, mint tea is poured by the host from a tall pot held well above the glasses. The fall mixes the tea, gives it air and raises the froth that a good pour should show on every glass, and the host fills the glasses in turn so each has the same strength.
